verses.2: Surely you are the people, and with you wisdom will perish.
verses.3: But I also have a heart, like any of you, and I was not born to be lesser than you. And who is there like you?
verses.4: You who mock your friend, who laugh at God—will the righteous be mocked and remain whole?
verses.5: Surely the lamp is for the wicked, and the fire is for those who cause trouble.
verses.6: The tents of robbers are left to desolation; and those who provoke God are crushed in their confidence, for God has placed them in his hand.
verses.7: But ask the beasts, and they will teach you; the birds of the sky will tell you.
verses.8: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; the fish of the sea will declare it to you.
verses.9: Who among all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
verses.10: In whose hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of every human being.
verses.11: Does not the ear test the words, and the mouth taste its food?
verses.12: Wisdom belongs to the aged, and understanding to those who live long.
verses.13: With him is wisdom and power, to him belong insight and understanding.
verses.14: He breaks down and builds up no one; he closes a man’s way and does not open it.
verses.15: He withholds the waters and they dry up; he releases them and they flood the land.
verses.16: With him is might and insight; to him belong the erring and the wise.
verses.17: He makes counselors wander, and judges are turned into fools.
verses.18: He removes the belt from kings, and binds their waist with a rope.
verses.19: He leads priests away as captives, and the strong are shattered.
verses.20: He takes away speech from the faithful and takes away understanding from the elders.
verses.21: He pours contempt on nobles and makes the mighty powerless.
verses.22: He reveals secrets from darkness and brings out the shadow of death into the light.
verses.23: He exalts nations, and then lays them waste; he crushes nations and brings them to rest.
verses.24: He turns the hearts of leaders of the earth, and makes them wander in a way they do not know.
verses.25: They grope in darkness with no light and stumble like a drunkard.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: "crushed in their confidence" reflects the Hebrew context of "battlements" and "those who provoke God," suggesting a loss of assurance rather than literal destruction.
- v. 23: "brings them to rest" translates the ambiguous Hebrew term יַנְחֵם, which may mean to comfort or to rest, chosen here to parallel the meaning of destruction in the first half.
- v. 24: "makes them wander in a way they do not know" captures the Hebrew לֹא־דָֽרֶךְ, which is a rare phrase meaning "not the way" or "unknown way."
